title: mcp.task.v1: an MCP Task, derived from a turn or a run
description: How the Control MCP server answers for a Task. A Task is not stored anywhere of its own: it is DERIVED, at the moment it is asked for, from the daemon's records, so it survives a restart of the MCP server and of the daemon. This record is that derivation; the server maps its fields onto the wire names of the protocol version it speaks (in the '2025-06-18' version the same facts are returned by the plain start, status and stop tools; in the '2026-07-28' version by the Tasks methods). A Task of a session is derived from a TURN, never from the run's last result, because several turns can share one run: task_id is the turn_id, status comes from the turn's state and outcome, result is the turn's own result, and expires_at is the turn's. The derivation for a turn: queued or running with no approval pending -> 'working'; an approval pending for it -> 'input_required'; state 'ended' (outcome candidate_done, done, waiting or paused) -> 'completed', with the outcome carried here so a caller can tell 'done' from 'waiting'; 'failed' -> 'failed'; 'interrupted' or 'stopped' -> 'cancelled'. A Task of a run started with run.start, which has no session and so no turn record, is derived from the run: task_id is the run_id; starting, running or unknown -> 'working' (an approval pending -> 'input_required'); ended with a result whose code is null -> 'completed'; ended with a code, start_failed or lost_reboot -> 'failed'; stopped -> 'cancelled'; its result is the run's result and it does not expire. A cancel is a Stop: it answers 'pending' until the Stop is confirmed, and while it is pending the status stays as it was and cancel_requested is true. 'cancelled' is shown only after the Stop is confirmed, never before. An approval is never answered through a Task: 'input_required' tells the client that a person must answer on a surface that draws approvals.

task_id.description: A turn_id or a run_id, as 'of' says.

of.description: What the Task is derived from.

outcome.description: The turn's outcome once it has ended; null before that, and always null for a Task of a run.

cancel_requested.description: True while a Stop has been asked and is not confirmed.

expires_at.description: The turn's expires_at: when its result can no longer be read. null means for as long as the record is kept.

poll_interval_ms.description: How long a client should wait before asking again; null when the daemon gives no advice.

result.description: The turn's result as the session record keeps it (or, for a Task of a run, the run's result in the same shape).
